enhanced.fullText:
The Protection of Human Subjects Regulations, commonly known as the Common Rule, establishes comprehensive federal standards for the ethical conduct of human subjects research across all federal departments and agencies. Codified primarily in 45 CFR Part 46, with parallel regulations across multiple agencies including 21 CFR Parts 50 and 56 for FDA-regulated research, these regulations mandate that higher education institutions receiving federal funding maintain robust oversight systems to protect research participants.

Under 45 CFR § 46.103, institutions must file a written Federal-wide Assurance (FWA) with the Office for Human Research Protections (OHRP), committing to comply with all Common Rule requirements. This assurance must designate one or more Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) and establish written procedures for prompt reporting of unanticipated problems, serious or continuing noncompliance, and suspension or termination of IRB approval.

The cornerstone requirement under 45 CFR § 46.109 mandates that all human subjects research undergo prospective IRB review and approval before commencement, unless specifically exempt under 45 CFR § 46.104. IRBs must include at least five members with varying backgrounds, including at least one scientist, one non-scientist, and one member unaffiliated with the institution, ensuring diverse expertise in research methodology and community standards.

Informed consent requirements under 45 CFR § 46.116, substantially revised effective January 19, 2018, require investigators to obtain and document voluntary informed consent from research participants using clear, understandable language. The revised regulations emphasize key information presentation, including research purpose, duration, procedures, reasonably foreseeable risks, and contact information for questions about rights and research-related injuries.

A critical 2020 amendment under 45 CFR § 46.114 established the single IRB requirement for multi-site research conducted within the United States, mandating use of one IRB for cooperative research involving multiple institutions, with limited exceptions for research not funded by a Common Rule agency or involving only publicly available data.

Violations can result in suspension or termination of federal funding, restriction of future funding eligibility, and referral to other agencies for potential civil or criminal prosecution. OHRP conducts compliance oversight through site visits, investigation of allegations, and mandatory reporting reviews, making institutional compliance programs essential for maintaining federal research funding eligibility.
enhanced.summary: Federal regulations requiring higher education institutions to establish IRB oversight systems, obtain informed consent for human subjects research, file federal assurances, and implement comprehensive reporting procedures to protect research participants and maintain federal funding eligibility.
enhanced.requirements:
## IRB Establishment and Operations
- Designate IRBs with minimum five members including scientist, non-scientist, and unaffiliated member per 45 CFR § 46.107
- Conduct prospective review of all human subjects research under 45 CFR § 46.109
- Document approval decisions with written determinations and risk assessments

## Federal Assurance Compliance
- File and maintain current Federal-wide Assurance (FWA) with OHRP per 45 CFR § 46.103
- Establish written procedures for reporting unanticipated problems within specified timeframes
- Designate institutional officials responsible for research oversight

## Informed Consent Documentation
- Obtain voluntary informed consent using revised elements per 45 CFR § 46.116
- Present key information prominently including risks, benefits, and contact information
- Document consent using signed forms or approved alternative procedures

## Single IRB Coordination
- Use single IRB for multi-site U.S. research per 45 CFR § 46.114 (effective January 2020)
- Establish reliance agreements and communication protocols between institutions
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Report unanticipated problems and serious noncompliance to IRB, institutional officials, and OHRP within institutional timeframes specified in FWA. Submit continuing review reports at intervals not exceeding one year per 45 CFR § 46.109(e). File FWA renewals every five years with OHRP.
